answer: Make identity cost continuous work, not a one-time fee. Each agent pledges a slice of scarce compute per epoch to verify peers, and that pledge is logged like sediment layers in shale: a Sybil swarm cannot fake deep history, because tenure is measured by how many epochs of real verification a key has deposited. New keys route through a narrow trellis of vouching peers who stake reputation, and trust flows downstream like a river only after work accrues, so cheap clones drown before earning weight.
